strengths: Well-motivated problem with rigorous motivational study (Section 2.2) demonstrating clear limitations of existing T2I methods through concrete examples
Practical modular design using lightweight adapter to avoid retraining frozen diffusion backbones, enabling efficient cross-domain transfer
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across three diverse domains (synthetic, facial, medical) with multiple complementary metrics (effectiveness, composition, realism, minimality)
Strong empirical results: 91% MAE reduction on Pendulum, 86% LPIPS on CelebA, 87% FID on ADNI; competitive or superior to baselines
Thoughtful technical design: Prompt-Aligned Injection creatively maps scalar attributes to learned token embeddings to address numeric-spatial alignment
Thorough ablation studies quantifying contribution of PAI and CTC regularizers
Good reproducibility support with detailed hyperparameters, algorithm descriptions, and promised code release
Honest limitations discussion acknowledging evaluation failures in OOD settings with concrete examples
weaknesses: Incomplete comparison with recent diffusion-based baselines: Main results omit DiffSCM, Pan & Bareinboim 2024, and Rasal et al. 2025; only CausalDiffAE and DisDiffAE included for Pendulum/CelebA, undermining 'state-of-the-art' claims
Strong unexamined assumption of known causal graphs G—no robustness analysis of graph misspecification; severely limits real-world applicability where causal structures are typically unknown

Limited theoretical justification for regularization strategies: Why PAI solves alignment and why CTC's inter/intra-token separation achieves causal disentanglement are asserted rather than formally justified; no theoretical guarantees
Causal mechanism identifiability not discussed: MLE fitting (Eq. 3) requires unstated assumptions; additive noise model (Eq. 2) may be too restrictive for complex causal relationships

Evaluation relies entirely on classifiers: No human evaluation for subjective quality; pre-trained classifiers have known biases and OOD failure modes; CLD metric validity (unconditional VAE latent distance) is questionable for semantic minimality
No cross-domain generalization testing: All experiments train and test within same domain, limiting evidence of robustness

Limited conceptual novelty: Individual components established (adapter-based guidance, contrastive disentanglement, SCM counterfactuals); contribution is primarily in combination/application rather than new methodology or theoretical insights
Hyperparameter sensitivity under-explored: Guidance scale α, CTC temperature τ, and scaling λ lack principled selection strategies; Table 6 shows α sensitivity but no guidance on selection
Attention Guidance appears orthogonal to core method: Sometimes degrades performance (Table 8), suggesting method robustness issues; feels like post-hoc technique rather than core contribution

Missing implementation details: How are attributes Y extracted/labeled for ADNI? Which validation set for hyperparameter tuning? No discussion of label quality assurance or sensitivity to annotation accuracy

strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear demonstration of limitations of existing T2I methods through systematic motivational study
Practical modular design that works with frozen diffusion models across multiple architectures (SD1.5, DiT, SD3) without retraining
Comprehensive experimental validation across diverse datasets (Pendulum, CelebA, ADNI) with systematic evaluation on four complementary metrics and multiple baselines
Thorough ablation studies clearly demonstrating the necessity and contribution of proposed regularization techniques (PAI: +11.6% F1, CTC: improved disentanglement)
Strong quantitative results with significant improvements: 91% MAE reduction on Pendulum, 87% FID reduction on ADNI, 86% LPIPS reduction on CelebA
Extensive supplementary material with detailed implementation, additional experiments (causal discovery, stress tests, generalization to SD3), and careful treatment of assumptions
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: core components (adapter architecture, PAI mechanism, CTC loss) are straightforward applications of existing techniques; main contribution is their combination with SCM, which is incremental

Strong assumption of known causal graph significantly limits practical applicability; robustness to graph misspecification not thoroughly analyzed; assumption acknowledged but not adequately addressed in limitations
Counterfactual identifiability not formally guaranteed due to approximate DDIM inversion; the method cannot ensure recovery of true exogenous noise, undermining causal validity claims

Weak theoretical justification for why proposed regularization strategies work: no principled explanation for PAI-induced disentanglement or theoretical analysis of CTC's effectiveness on token separation

Evaluation lacks human studies critical for assessing visual quality and counterfactual faithfulness; reliance on pretrained classifiers for effectiveness metrics introduces potential bias; FID and CLD metrics computed in proxy spaces that may not reflect true causal relationships
Limited failure analysis: all presented results appear successful with no discussion of failure modes, edge cases with complex attribute interactions, or performance degradation scenarios

Incomplete comparisons: motivational study compares with general editing methods (NTI, MCPL) rather than counterfactual approaches; DiffCounter comparison limited to CelebA-HQ; some recent counterfactual methods not included

Computational efficiency not discussed: inference time not compared to baselines; training time and parameter overhead not analyzed; hyperparameter choices (λ=0.0005, τ=0.2) appear arbitrary without sensitivity analysis
